- 
+ # Email Parsing and ATS Scoring Scripts
+ 
+ This directory contains scripts for parsing email messages (&#96;.msg&#96; files) and analyzing them for ATS (Application for Teile und Stoffe / Application for Parts and Substances) applications.
+ 
+ ## Overview
+ 
+ The scripts in this directory work together to:
+ 1. Parse Outlook &#96;.msg&#96; files and extract metadata
+ 2. Score emails for ATS application probability
+ 3. Generate reports on email analysis
+ 
+ ## Scripts
+ 
+ ### &#96;mailparser.py&#96;
+ **Purpose**: Basic email metadata extraction
+ 
+ Parses all &#96;.msg&#96; files from a specified directory tree and extracts basic metadata:
+ - Email subject
+ - Sender address
+ - Attachment filenames
+ - Path to the folder containing the email
+ 
+ **Output**: &#96;parsed_messages.json&#96; - A JSON file containing an array of email metadata objects.
+ 
+ **Usage**: 
+ - Modify &#96;ROOT_FOLDER&#96; variable to point to your email directory
+ - Run the script to generate &#96;parsed_messages.json&#96;
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### &#96;mailscorer.py&#96;
+ **Purpose**: Parse and score emails for ATS probability
+ 
+ Combines email parsing with ATS scoring. This script:
+ - Walks through a directory of &#96;.msg&#96; files
+ - Extracts email metadata (subject, sender, attachments)
+ - Scores each email for ATS application probability using keyword matching and attachment pattern recognition
+ - Outputs results with detailed scoring breakdown
+ 
+ **Scoring Logic**:
+ - **High keywords** (10 points): &quot;antrag&quot;, &quot;ats&quot;, &quot;afts&quot;, &quot;teile und stoffe&quot;, etc.
+ - **Medium keywords** (3 points): &quot;freigabe&quot;, &quot;approval&quot;, &quot;material&quot;, etc.
+ - **Attachment patterns**:
+   - ATS forms: +15 points
+   - Safety Data Sheets (SDS): +8 points
+   - Technical Data Sheets (TDS): +5 points
+   - Bonus: +10 points if both ATS form and data sheets present
+ - **Ignore rules**: Emails from specific senders or with certain subjects are penalized (-100 points)
+ 
+ **Output**: &#96;ats-scores.json&#96; - JSON file with email data and ATS scoring results.
+ 
+ **Usage**:
+ - Modify &#96;ROOT_DIR&#96; variable to point to your email directory
+ - Run the script to generate scored results
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### &#96;scorer.py&#96;
+ **Purpose**: Comprehensive ATS email scoring with report generation
+ 
+ A more advanced scoring system that works with JSON email data files. This script provides:
+ - Detailed scoring of email subject, body, and attachments
+ - Probability classification (HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, NONE)
+ - Detailed reasoning for each score
+ - Report generation functionality
+ 
+ **Features**:
+ - Works with pre-extracted email JSON files (e.g., &#96;emails_inbox.json&#96;)
+ - Handles multiple file encodings (UTF-8, Latin1, CP1252)
+ - Generates detailed text reports with statistics
+ - Identifies high-probability ATS applications
+ 
+ **Output**: 
+ - Console output with summary statistics
+ - &#96;ats_email_analysis_report.txt&#96; - Detailed report file
+ 
+ **Usage**:
+ - Ensure you have an email JSON file (the script searches multiple possible paths)
+ - Run the script to analyze emails and generate a report
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### &#96;msgparser.py&#96;
+ **Purpose**: Parse and split individual &#96;.msg&#96; files
+ 
+ Utility script for parsing a single &#96;.msg&#96; file:
+ - Extracts HTML body content
+ - Splits HTML body into separate parts (based on email thread separators)
+ - Extracts and saves all attachments
+ 
+ **Output**: 
+ - &#96;output/message_part_*.html&#96; - Individual HTML parts of the email
+ - &#96;output/attachments/&#96; - Directory containing all email attachments
+ 
+ **Usage**:
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ python msgparser.py &lt;path_to_msg_file&gt;
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### &#96;fromwho.py&#96;
+ **Purpose**: Documentation for ongoing ATS application detection
+ 
+ This file contains documentation and planning notes for detecting ongoing ATS applications at different stages of the approval workflow. It describes:
+ - The ATS application workflow stages (6 stages from incoming application to final approval)
+ - Department email addresses involved in the process
+ - Detection criteria for each stage (ChemScan, UWS, HSE OU/DW, LAB OU/DW)
+ 
+ **Status**: Currently contains documentation/comments only - implementation pending.
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### &#96;emailer.py&#96;
+ **Purpose**: Path configuration
+ 
+ Contains path definitions for email data files:
+ - &#96;inbox_json_path&#96; - Path to the email inbox JSON file
+ - &#96;email_data_files&#96; - Path to the email data directory
+ 
+ **Status**: Configuration file with path definitions.
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ## Workflow
+ 
+ A typical workflow might be:
+ 
+ 1. **Extract emails**: Use &#96;mailparser.py&#96; to extract basic metadata from &#96;.msg&#96; files
+ 2. **Score emails**: Use &#96;mailscorer.py&#96; or &#96;scorer.py&#96; to analyze emails for ATS probability
+ 3. **Review results**: Check the generated JSON files or reports to identify high-probability ATS applications
+ 4. **Parse specific emails**: Use &#96;msgparser.py&#96; to extract attachments and split email threads from specific &#96;.msg&#96; files
+ 
+ ## Dependencies
+ 
+ - &#96;extract_msg&#96; - For parsing Outlook &#96;.msg&#96; files
+ - Standard Python libraries: &#96;json&#96;, &#96;os&#96;, &#96;re&#96;, &#96;typing&#96;, &#96;pathlib&#96;
+ 
+ ## Output Files
+ 
+ - &#96;parsed_messages.json&#96; - Basic email metadata (from &#96;mailparser.py&#96;)
+ - &#96;ats-scores.json&#96; - Email data with ATS scores (from &#96;mailscorer.py&#96;)
+ - &#96;ats_email_analysis_report.txt&#96; - Detailed scoring report (from &#96;scorer.py&#96;)
+ - &#96;output/&#96; - Directory for parsed email parts and attachments (from &#96;msgparser.py&#96;)
+ 
+ ## Notes
+ 
+ - All scripts expect &#96;.msg&#96; files (Outlook message format)
+ - Paths are hardcoded in some scripts and may need to be adjusted for your environment
+ - The scoring system is designed to identify new incoming ATS applications and filter out internal communications
+ 
```

+ &quot;&quot;&quot;
+ Single .msg file ATS probability scorer.
+ 
+ This module provides functionality to parse a single Outlook .msg file
+ and score it for ATS (Application for Teile und Stoffe) probability.
+ &quot;&quot;&quot;
+ 
+ import os
+ import re
+ from typing import Dict, List, Optional
+ import extract_msg
+ 
+ 
+ class ATSEmailScorer:
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;Scores emails for ATS (Application for Teile und Stoffe) probability.&quot;&quot;&quot;
+     
+     def __init__(self):
+         # High probability keywords (case insensitive)
+         self.high_keywords = [
+             &#39;antrag&#39;, &#39;ats&#39;, &#39;afts&#39;, &#39;aft&amp;s&#39;, &#39;aftus&#39;, 
+             &#39;antrag teile und stoffe&#39;, &#39;antrag für teile und stoffe&#39;,
+             &#39;teile und stoffe&#39;, &#39;application materials&#39;
+         ]
+         
+         # Medium probability keywords
+         self.medium_keywords = [
+             &#39;freigabe&#39;, &#39;approval&#39;, &#39;genehmigung&#39;, &#39;zulassung&#39;,
+             &#39;material&#39;, &#39;substance&#39;, &#39;chemical&#39;, &#39;produkt&#39;
+         ]
+         
+         # Attachment filename patterns for ATS forms
+         self.ats_patterns = [
+             r&#39;.*ats.*&#39;, r&#39;.*afts.*&#39;, r&#39;.*aft&amp;s.*&#39;, r&#39;.*antrag.*&#39;,
+             r&#39;.*teile.*stoffe.*&#39;, r&#39;.*application.*&#39;
+         ]
+         
+         # Safety Data Sheet patterns
+         self.sds_patterns = [
+             r&#39;.*sdb.*&#39;, r&#39;.*msds.*&#39;, r&#39;.*sds.*&#39;, r&#39;.*safety.*data.*sheet.*&#39;
+         ]
+         
+         # Technical/Product Data Sheet patterns
+         self.tds_patterns = [
+             r&#39;.*pdb.*&#39;, r&#39;.*tdb.*&#39;, r&#39;.*tds.*&#39;, r&#39;.*pds.*&#39;,
+             r&#39;.*technical.*data.*sheet.*&#39;, r&#39;.*product.*data.*sheet.*&#39;
+         ]
+         
+         # Email addresses to ignore (our own emails)
+         self.ignore_senders = [
+             &#39;irm-standartization-office@rolls-royce.com&#39;
+         ]
+         
+         # Subject patterns to ignore
+         self.ignore_subjects = [
+             &#39;qctp&#39;, &#39;pbr&#39;, &#39;din&#39;, &#39;rqsc&#39;, &#39;ballot&#39;, &#39;la&#39;, &#39;edns&#39;
+         ]
+     
+     def score_email(self, subject: str, sender: str, attachments: List[str]) -&gt; Dict:
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         Score an email for ATS probability.
+         
+         Args:
+             subject: Email subject line
+             sender: Email sender address
+             attachments: List of attachment filenames
+             
+         Returns:
+             Dictionary containing:
+             - total_score: Total numerical score
+             - probability: &quot;HIGH&quot;, &quot;MEDIUM&quot;, &quot;LOW&quot;, or &quot;NONE&quot;
+             - is_ats_application: Boolean indicating if this is likely an ATS application
+             - reasoning: List of strings explaining the score
+             - details: Dictionary with score breakdown
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;
+         subj_l = subject.lower()
+         sender_l = sender.lower()
+         attachments_l = [a.lower() for a in attachments]
+         
+         scores = {
+             &quot;subject_score&quot;: 0.0,
+             &quot;body_score&quot;: 0.0,  # Not available from .msg-only parsing
+             &quot;attachment_score&quot;: 0.0,
+             &quot;sender_penalty&quot;: 0.0,
+             &quot;ignore_penalty&quot;: 0.0
+         }
+         reasoning = []
+         
+         # Ignore rules
+         if any(ignore in sender_l for ignore in self.ignore_senders) or \
+            any(ignore in subj_l for ignore in self.ignore_subjects):
+             scores[&quot;ignore_penalty&quot;] = -100.0
+             reasoning.append(&quot;Email ignored due to sender or subject.&quot;)
+             return self._format_result(scores, reasoning, subject, sender)
+         
+         # Subject scoring
+         for kw in self.high_keywords:
+             if kw in subj_l:
+                 scores[&quot;subject_score&quot;] += 10.0
+         for kw in self.medium_keywords:
+             if kw in subj_l:
+                 scores[&quot;subject_score&quot;] += 3.0
+         if scores[&quot;subject_score&quot;]:
+             reasoning.append(f&quot;Subject contains ATS-related keywords (score: {scores[&#39;subject_score&#39;]:.1f})&quot;)
+         
+         # Attachment scoring
+         ats, sds, tds = False, False, False
+         for fname in attachments_l:
+             if any(re.match(pat, fname) for pat in self.ats_patterns):
+                 scores[&quot;attachment_score&quot;] += 15.0
+                 ats = True
+             elif any(re.match(pat, fname) for pat in self.sds_patterns):
+                 scores[&quot;attachment_score&quot;] += 8.0
+                 sds = True
+             elif any(re.match(pat, fname) for pat in self.tds_patterns):
+                 scores[&quot;attachment_score&quot;] += 5.0
+                 tds = True
+         
+         if attachments:
+             scores[&quot;attachment_score&quot;] += 2.0  # Base bonus for having attachments
+         
+         if ats and (sds or tds):
+             scores[&quot;attachment_score&quot;] += 10.0  # Bonus for having both form and data sheets
+         
+         if scores[&quot;attachment_score&quot;]:
+             reasoning.append(f&quot;Attachments suggest ATS content (score: {scores[&#39;attachment_score&#39;]:.1f})&quot;)
+         
+         return self._format_result(scores, reasoning, subject, sender)
+     
+     def _format_result(self, scores: Dict, reasoning: List[str], subject: str, sender: str) -&gt; Dict:
+         &quot;&quot;&quot;Format the scoring result into a structured dictionary.&quot;&quot;&quot;
+         total = sum(scores.values())
+         
+         if scores[&quot;ignore_penalty&quot;] &lt; 0:
+             prob, is_ats = &quot;NONE&quot;, False
+         elif total &gt;= 20.0:
+             prob, is_ats = &quot;HIGH&quot;, True
+         elif total &gt;= 10.0:
+             prob, is_ats = &quot;MEDIUM&quot;, False
+         elif total &gt;= 3.0:
+             prob, is_ats = &quot;LOW&quot;, False
+         else:
+             prob, is_ats = &quot;NONE&quot;, False
+         
+         return {
+             &quot;total_score&quot;: total,
+             &quot;probability&quot;: prob,
+             &quot;is_ats_application&quot;: is_ats,
+             &quot;reasoning&quot;: reasoning if reasoning else [&quot;No strong ATS indicators.&quot;],
+             &quot;details&quot;: scores,
+             &quot;subject&quot;: subject,
+             &quot;sender&quot;: sender
+         }
+ 
+ 
+ def score_msg_file(msg_path: str) -&gt; Optional[Dict]:
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     Parse and score a single .msg file for ATS probability.
+     
+     Args:
+         msg_path: Path to the .msg file
+         
+     Returns:
+         Dictionary containing email metadata and ATS score, or None if parsing fails.
+         Structure:
+         {
+             &quot;subject&quot;: str,
+             &quot;sender&quot;: str,
+             &quot;attachments&quot;: List[str],
+             &quot;ats_score&quot;: {
+                 &quot;total_score&quot;: float,
+                 &quot;probability&quot;: str,
+                 &quot;is_ats_application&quot;: bool,
+                 &quot;reasoning&quot;: List[str],
+                 &quot;details&quot;: Dict
+             }
+         }
+         
+     Raises:
+         FileNotFoundError: If the .msg file doesn&#39;t exist
+         Exception: If there&#39;s an error parsing the .msg file
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     if not os.path.exists(msg_path):
+         raise FileNotFoundError(f&quot;Message file not found: {msg_path}&quot;)
+     
+     if not msg_path.lower().endswith(&#39;.msg&#39;):
+         raise ValueError(f&quot;File is not a .msg file: {msg_path}&quot;)
+     
+     try:
+         # Parse the .msg file
+         msg = extract_msg.Message(msg_path)
+         
+         # Extract email data
+         subject = msg.subject or &quot;&quot;
+         sender = msg.sender or &quot;&quot;
+         attachments = [
+             att.longFilename or att.shortFilename or f&quot;attachment_{i+1}&quot;
+             for i, att in enumerate(msg.attachments)
+         ]
+         
+         # Score the email
+         scorer = ATSEmailScorer()
+         score_data = scorer.score_email(subject, sender, attachments)
+         
+         return {
+             &quot;subject&quot;: subject,
+             &quot;sender&quot;: sender,
+             &quot;attachments&quot;: attachments,
+             &quot;msg_path&quot;: msg_path,
+             &quot;ats_score&quot;: score_data
+         }
+         
+     except Exception as e:
+         raise Exception(f&quot;Error parsing {msg_path}: {e}&quot;)
+ 
+ 
+ def print_score_summary(result: Dict):
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     Print a human-readable summary of the scoring result.
+     
+     Args:
+         result: Result dictionary from score_msg_file()
+     &quot;&quot;&quot;
+     if result is None:
+         print(&quot;No result to display.&quot;)
+         return
+     
+     print(&quot;=&quot; * 60)
+     print(&quot;ATS EMAIL SCORE SUMMARY&quot;)
+     print(&quot;=&quot; * 60)
+     print(f&quot;Subject: {result[&#39;subject&#39;]}&quot;)
+     print(f&quot;Sender: {result[&#39;sender&#39;]}&quot;)
+     print(f&quot;Attachments: {len(result[&#39;attachments&#39;])}&quot;)
+     if result[&#39;attachments&#39;]:
+         for att in result[&#39;attachments&#39;]:
+             print(f&quot;  - {att}&quot;)
+     
+     score = result[&#39;ats_score&#39;]
+     print(f&quot;\nTotal Score: {score[&#39;total_score&#39;]:.1f}&quot;)
+     print(f&quot;Probability: {score[&#39;probability&#39;]}&quot;)
+     print(f&quot;ATS Application: {&#39;YES&#39; if score[&#39;is_ats_application&#39;] else &#39;NO&#39;}&quot;)
+     
+     print(&quot;\nScore Breakdown:&quot;)
+     for key, value in score[&#39;details&#39;].items():
+         if value != 0:
+             print(f&quot;  {key}: {value:.1f}&quot;)
+     
+     print(&quot;\nReasoning:&quot;)
+     for reason in score[&#39;reasoning&#39;]:
+         print(f&quot;  - {reason}&quot;)
+     print(&quot;=&quot; * 60)
+ 
+ 
+ # ========== MAIN ==========
+ if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
+     import sys
+     
+     if len(sys.argv) != 2:
+         print(&quot;Usage: python score_msg.py &lt;path_to_msg_file&gt;&quot;)
+         sys.exit(1)
+     
+     msg_file = sys.argv[1]
+     
+     try:
+         result = score_msg_file(msg_file)
+         print_score_summary(result)
+     except Exception as e:
+         print(f&quot;Error: {e}&quot;, file=sys.stderr)
+         sys.exit(1)
+ 
```

Created `score_msg.py`, a module for scoring a single `.msg` file for ATS probability.

## Features

1. **Standalone module** — Can be imported or run as a script
2. **Single file scoring** — Takes a path to one `.msg` file and returns a score
3. **Structured output** — Returns a dictionary with:
   - Email metadata (subject, sender, attachments)
   - ATS score (total score, probability, reasoning, breakdown)
4. **Error handling** — Validates file existence and handles parsing errors
5. **Summary printing** — Includes a function to print human-readable summaries

## Usage Examples

**As a script:**
```bash
python score_msg.py path/to/email.msg
```

**As a module:**
```python
from score_msg import score_msg_file, print_score_summary

result = score_msg_file("email.msg")
print_score_summary(result)
```

The module uses the same scoring logic as `mailscorer.py` (keyword matching, attachment pattern recognition, ignore rules) but is focused on single-file processing. The README has been updated to document this new module.

Current scoring method:

1. Keywords only (subject line):
   - High keywords: "antrag", "ats", "afts", "teile und stoffe" → +10 points each
   - Medium keywords: "freigabe", "approval", "material" → +3 points each

2. Attachment filename patterns (not content):
   - Regex on filenames only (e.g., `.*ats.*`, `.*sds.*`)
   - No PDF content analysis

3. No distinction between NEW vs ONGOING:
   - Doesn't detect ATS numbers (XXX-YYYY format)
   - Doesn't identify workflow stages
   - Doesn't check sender departments

Limitations:
- No PDF content analysis: only filenames are checked
- No NEW vs ONGOING detection: can't tell if it's a new application or part of an existing workflow

Enhancing the module to:
1. Extract and analyze PDF content (if attachments are available)
2. Detect NEW vs ONGOING applications
3. Identify workflow stages

- Filename patterns: 15 points for ATS forms, 8 for SDS, 5 for TDS

## Your Proposed Approach vs Current README

**Your 3-stage approach:**
1. **ATS Detector** (lightweight) → Fast filtering
2. **NEW vs ONGOING Detector** (heavier) → Only for ATS emails
3. **Workflow Routing** → Different pipelines

**Current README structure:**
- 1.1 ATS detector (basic)
- 1.2 Stage detector (but doesn't distinguish NEW vs ONGOING clearly)
- 1.3 Download/Extract
- Then PDF analysis, Excel, etc.

## Recommended Refinement

Refine the README workflow to match your approach:

```
1. Email (In)

1.1. ATS Detector (Lightweight Filter)
    - Subject keywords
    - Attachment filename patterns
    - Sender filtering
    → Output: ATS_PROBABILITY (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/NONE)
    → If NONE: Stop processing, archive email
    
1.2. NEW vs ONGOING Classifier (Only if ATS_PROBABILITY >= MEDIUM)
    - Extract attachments to staging area
    - PDF content analysis:
        * Check if ATS form exists and is valid
        * Check if ATS number (XXX-YYYY) exists in form/subject
        * Check if TKZ (XXXXXXXX) exists
        * Check which fields are filled (applicant-only vs department signatures)
    - Sender analysis:
        * Applicant domain → likely NEW
        * Department senders (UUB, UWS, HSE, LAB) → likely ONGOING
    - Body content patterns (for stage-specific detection)
    → Output: CLASSIFICATION (NEW | ONGOING_STAGE_X | UNKNOWN)
    
1.3. Workflow Router
    → Route based on CLASSIFICATION:
        - NEW → Pipeline A (Initial processing)
        - ONGOING_STAGE_X → Pipeline B (Stage-specific processing)
        - UNKNOWN → Manual review queue
```

## Pipeline Differences

**NEW Application Pipeline:**
- PDF analysis (extract all fields)
- Excel lookup (check for duplicates)
- Generate ATS number + TKZ
- Validate completeness (SDS, TDS, COC requirements)
- Generate response email if missing info
- Excel write (create new entry)
- PDF write (fill in IDs)
- File operations (rename, organize)
- Email (Out) to next stage

**ONGOING Application Pipeline:**
- Identify current stage (from sender/body/attachments)
- PDF analysis (extract updated fields, signatures)
- Excel lookup (find existing entry by ATS number)
- Excel write (update status, add signatures)
- PDF write (update form with new signatures/evaluations)
- File operations (update existing files)
- Email (Out) to next stage (or completion)

2. For ONGOING, should we detect the specific stage (UUB, UWS, HSE, LAB) in 1.2, or defer to later?
3. Should "UNKNOWN" emails go to a manual review queue, or attempt auto-classification with lower confidence?
4. Should PDF analysis happen in 1.2 (for classification) or later in the pipeline (for data extraction)?

This keeps the fast filter first, then heavier processing only for ATS emails, with clear routing. Should I update the README to reflect this structure?

## Refined 3-Stage Approach Based on Documentation

### **Stage 1: ATS Detector (Lightweight - Fast Filter)**
**Purpose**: Quick filter to identify ATS-related emails

**Checks**:
- Subject keywords: "Antrag", "ATS", "AfTS", "Teile und Stoffe"
- Attachment filename patterns: `.*ats.*`, `.*sds.*`, `.*tds.*`
- Sender filtering: Ignore internal standardization office emails

**Output**: `ATS_PROBABILITY` (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/NONE)
- If NONE → Stop, archive email
- If HIGH/MEDIUM → Proceed to Stage 2

---

### **Stage 2: NEW vs ONGOING Classifier (Heavy Processing)**
**Purpose**: Distinguish new applications from workflow emails

**Extract attachments first** (needed for PDF analysis)

**NEW Application Indicators** (from T00221 form analysis):
1. **Field 1 (Request No.)**: Empty or not in XXX/YYYY format
2. **Field 5**: "New Demand" checked (vs "Change in Demand")
3. **Field 20**: Empty (no reference to past requests)
4. **Field 51 (TKZ)**: Empty (not yet assigned)
5. **Form completion**: Only Fields 2-21 filled (applicant section), Fields 22-50 empty
6. **Sender**: From applicant domain (not department emails)
7. **Subject**: Basic keywords without ATS number pattern

**ONGOING Application Indicators**:
1. **Field 1**: Contains ATS number (XXX/YYYY format) - already assigned
2. **Field 5**: "Change in Demand" OR Field 20 references previous ATS
3. **Field 51**: Contains TKZ (XXXXXXXX format) - already assigned
4. **Form completion**: Department fields filled (22-50 have signatures)
5. **Sender**: Department emails:
   - `gefahrstoffmanagement@uub-schwan.de` → ChemScan (Stage 2)
   - `karsten.bartz@rolls-royce.com` → UWS (Stage 3)
   - `hse-newsou@rolls-royce.com` or `hs-e-teamdw@rolls-royce.com` → HSE (Stage 4)
   - `ralph.gross@rolls-royce.com` or `rrd-materials-spg@rolls-royce.com` → LAB (Stage 5)
   - `CBS-Standardisation-Office@Rolls-Royce.com` → Final approval (Stage 6)
6. **Subject**: Contains ATS number (XXX/YYYY) and/or TKZ (XXXXXXXX)
7. **Body patterns**: Stage-specific text (e.g., "ChemScan: Stellungnahmen", "der Teil Umweltschutz der Anträge ist bearbeitet")
8. **Attachments**: Version suffixes like " (002)" for UWS

**Output**: `CLASSIFICATION`
- `NEW` → Pipeline A (Initial processing)
- `ONGOING_STAGE_2` (ChemScan/UUB)
- `ONGOING_STAGE_3` (UWS)
- `ONGOING_STAGE_4` (HSE)
- `ONGOING_STAGE_5` (LAB)
- `ONGOING_STAGE_6` (Final approval)
- `UNKNOWN` → Manual review queue

---

### **Stage 3: Workflow Router**
**Purpose**: Route to appropriate processing pipeline

**NEW Application Pipeline** (from AAW11-03, Section 01-03):
1. Extract all form fields (2-21)
2. Validate completeness (SDS, TDS, required fields)
3. Check MLC132 (prohibited substances)
4. Excel lookup (check for duplicates in Verzeichnis.xlsb)
5. Generate ATS number (XXX/YYYY) from Verzeichnis.xlsb
6. Generate TKZ (0104XXXX) from Teilenummern 0104....xls
7. Generate response email if missing info
8. Excel write (create new entry in Verzeichnis.xlsb)
9. PDF write (fill Field 1 and Field 51)
10. File operations (organize attachments)
11. Email (Out) to applicant (confirmation) + start ChemScan request

**ONGOING Application Pipeline** (from AAW11-03, Section 04-10):
1. Identify current stage from sender/body/attachments
2. Extract updated fields and signatures from PDF
3. Excel lookup (find existing entry by ATS number)
4. Excel write (update status, add signatures)
5. PDF write (update form with new signatures/evaluations)
6. File operations (update existing files)
7. Email (Out) to next stage (or completion notification)

---

## Questions for Refinement

1. PDF analysis timing: Should we parse the ATS form PDF in Stage 2 (for classification) or defer to Stage 3 (for data extraction)? Recommendation: Light parsing in Stage 2 (check Field 1, 5, 20, 51, signature presence), full extraction in Stage 3.

2. Stage detection: Should Stage 2 detect the specific workflow stage (2-6) or just NEW vs ONGOING? Recommendation: Detect the specific stage in Stage 2 to route directly to the correct pipeline.

3. Confidence thresholds: What if classification is ambiguous? Recommendation: Use confidence scores and route low-confidence to manual review.

4. Change requests: Field 5 "Change in Demand" with Field 20 reference — treat as ONGOING or a special NEW variant? Recommendation: Treat as ONGOING since it references an existing ATS.

This aligns with the documented workflow. Should I update the README to reflect this structure?

## Refined 3-Stage Approach

### **Stage 1: ATS Detector (Lightweight Filter)**
**Output**: `ATS_PROBABILITY` (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/NONE)
- If NONE → Stop, archive
- If HIGH/MEDIUM → Proceed to Stage 2

---

### **Stage 2: Classification (NEW vs ONGOING + Stage Detection)**
**Purpose**: Single step that determines both NEW/ONGOING status and specific workflow stage

**Method**: Analyze PDF form completion level (which fields are filled)

**Classification Logic**:

1. **NEW ATS** (completely new materials):
   - Field 1 (Request No.): Empty or not assigned
   - Field 51 (TKZ): Empty or not assigned
   - Only Fields 2-21 filled (applicant section)
   - Fields 22-50 empty (no department signatures)
   - Sender: Applicant domain (not department)
   - Subject: Basic keywords, no ATS number pattern

2. **ONGOING_STAGE_2** (ChemScan/UUB):
   - Field 1: Has ATS number (XXX/YYYY)
   - Field 51: May or may not have TKZ yet
   - Fields 2-24 filled (applicant + ChemScan section)
   - Fields 25-50 empty
   - Sender: `gefahrstoffmanagement@uub-schwan.de` OR from Standardisation Office forwarding
   - Subject: May contain "ChemScan: Stellungnahmen"
   - Attachments: ChemScan report PDF

3. **ONGOING_STAGE_3** (UWS):
   - Fields 2-31 filled (applicant + ChemScan + UWS)
   - Fields 32-50 empty
   - Sender: `karsten.bartz@rolls-royce.com`
   - Body: "der Teil Umweltschutz der Anträge ist bearbeitet"
   - Attachments: May have " (002)" suffix

4. **ONGOING_STAGE_4** (HSE):
   - Fields 2-38 filled (applicant + ChemScan + UWS + HSE)
   - Fields 39-50 empty
   - Sender: `hse-newsou@rolls-royce.com` or `hs-e-teamdw@rolls-royce.com`
   - Body: "anbei die Freigabe" (OU) or "der Antrag ist bearbeitet und freigegeben" (DW)

5. **ONGOING_STAGE_5** (LAB):
   - Fields 2-49 filled (applicant + ChemScan + UWS + HSE + LAB)
   - Field 50 empty
   - Sender: `ralph.gross@rolls-royce.com` or `rrd-materials-spg@rolls-royce.com`

6. **ONGOING_STAGE_6** (Final Approval):
   - Fields 2-50 filled (all sections complete)
   - Sender: `CBS-Standardisation-Office@Rolls-Royce.com`
   - Ready for final release

7. **CHANGE** (inactive branch, keep in mind):
   - Field 1: Has ATS number
   - Field 5: "Change in Demand" checked
   - Field 20: References previous ATS
   - Field 51: Has TKZ
   - Same process flow but already has ATS/TKZ pair
   - Currently: Route to manual review or special handling

8. **UNKNOWN**:
   - Cannot determine classification
   - Route to manual review queue (HITL)

**Output**: `CLASSIFICATION` with confidence score
- `NEW` (confidence: 0.0-1.0)
- `ONGOING_STAGE_X` (confidence: 0.0-1.0)
- `CHANGE` (confidence: 0.0-1.0) - inactive
- `UNKNOWN` (confidence: <0.5) → Manual review

---

### **Stage 3: Workflow Router**
**Purpose**: Route to appropriate processing pipeline based on classification

**Routing**:
- `NEW` → Initial processing pipeline (assign ATS/TKZ, validate, start circulation)
- `ONGOING_STAGE_X` → Stage-specific processing (extract updates, update Excel, forward to next stage)
- `CHANGE` → Special handling (currently manual)
- `UNKNOWN` → Human review queue

**HITL Integration**:
- Low confidence (<0.7) → Flag for human review but still process
- Very low confidence (<0.5) → Manual review queue only
- Human can override classification in frontend (future: training data for improvement)

## Refined 3-Stage Approach

### **Stage 1: ATS Detector**
**Purpose**: Fast filter to identify ATS-related emails

**Checks**:
- Subject keywords: "Antrag", "ATS", "AfTS", "Teile und Stoffe"
- Attachment filename patterns: `.*ats.*`, `.*sds.*`, `.*tds.*`
- Sender filtering: Ignore internal standardization office emails

**Output**: `ATS_PROBABILITY` (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/NONE)
- If NONE → Stop, archive email
- If HIGH/MEDIUM → Proceed to Stage 2

---

### **Stage 2: Stage Detector**
**Purpose**: Classify email type and workflow stage

#### **2a. Type Classification** (NEW vs ONGOING vs CHANGE)

**NEW ATS**:
- Field 1 (Request No.): Empty or not assigned
- Field 51 (TKZ): Empty or not assigned
- Only Fields 2-21 filled (applicant section)
- Fields 22-50 empty
- Sender: Applicant domain
- Subject: Basic keywords, no ATS number

**ONGOING**:
- Field 1: Has ATS number (XXX/YYYY format)
- Field 51: May or may not have TKZ
- Fields 22+ have some signatures (workflow in progress)
- Sender: Department email OR Standardisation Office forwarding
- Subject: Contains ATS number and/or TKZ

**CHANGE**:
- Field 1: Has ATS number
- Field 5: "Change in Demand" checked
- Field 20: References previous ATS number
- Field 51: Has TKZ
- Currently: Flag/tag for future handling, ignore processing

**Output**: `TYPE` (NEW | ONGOING | CHANGE | UNKNOWN)

#### **2b. Ongoing Stage Detection** (only if TYPE = ONGOING)

**ONGOING_STAGE_2** (ChemScan/UUB):
- Fields 2-24 filled
- Fields 25-50 empty
- Sender: `gefahrstoffmanagement@uub-schwan.de`
- Subject: "ChemScan: Stellungnahmen"
- Attachments: ChemScan report PDF

**ONGOING_STAGE_3** (UWS):
- Fields 2-31 filled
- Fields 32-50 empty
- Sender: `karsten.bartz@rolls-royce.com`
- Body: "der Teil Umweltschutz der Anträge ist bearbeitet"

**ONGOING_STAGE_4** (HSE):
- Fields 2-38 filled
- Fields 39-50 empty
- Sender: `hse-newsou@rolls-royce.com` or `hs-e-teamdw@rolls-royce.com`

**ONGOING_STAGE_5** (LAB):
- Fields 2-49 filled
- Field 50 empty
- Sender: `ralph.gross@rolls-royce.com` or `rrd-materials-spg@rolls-royce.com`

**ONGOING_STAGE_6** (Final Approval):
- Fields 2-50 filled
- Sender: `CBS-Standardisation-Office@Rolls-Royce.com`

**Output**: `STAGE` (2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | UNKNOWN)

---

### **Stage 3: Workflow Router**
**Purpose**: Route to appropriate processing pipeline

**Routing Logic**:
- `TYPE = NEW` → `new_workflow` pipeline
- `TYPE = ONGOING` → `ongoing_workflow` with `STAGE` parameter
- `TYPE = CHANGE` → Flag/tag, ignore processing (future handling)
- `TYPE = UNKNOWN` → Manual review queue (HITL)

**Pipelines**:
- `new_workflow`: Initial processing (assign ATS/TKZ, validate, start circulation)
- `ongoing_workflow(STAGE_X)`: Stage-specific processing (extract updates, update Excel, forward to next stage)

+ ## Overview
+ 
+ This document describes the 3-stage email processing workflow for ATS (Antrag für Teile und Stoffe) applications. The workflow is designed to automatically classify and route emails through the appropriate processing pipelines.
+ 
+ ## Definitions
+ 
+ - **ATS**: Antrag für Teile und Stoffe (Application for Parts and Materials)
+ - **CMSR**: Consumables and Materials Supply Request
+ - **TKZ**: Teilkennzahl (Part Number)
+ - **HITL**: Human-In-The-Loop (manual review workflow)
+ 
+ ## Workflow Stages
+ 
+ The ATS approval process goes through 6 stages:
+ 
+ 1. **Applicant** - Initial application submission
+ 2. **UUB (ChemScan)** - Hazards assessment by Umwelt- und Unternehmensberatung Schwan
+ 3. **UWS** - Environment protection evaluation
+ 4. **HSE** - Health, Safety &amp; Environment evaluation
+ 5. **LAB** - Manufacturing Laboratory evaluation
+ 6. **NRM** - Standardization Office final approval
+ 
+ ## 3-Stage Email Processing Workflow
+ 
+ ### Stage 1: ATS Detector
+ 
+ **Purpose**: Fast, lightweight filter to identify ATS-related emails
+ 
+ **Processing**:
+ - Subject line keyword matching: &quot;Antrag&quot;, &quot;ATS&quot;, &quot;AfTS&quot;, &quot;Teile und Stoffe&quot;, etc.
+ - Attachment filename pattern matching: &#96;.*ats.*&#96;, &#96;.*sds.*&#96;, &#96;.*tds.*&#96;, etc.
+ - Sender filtering: Ignore internal standardization office emails
+ 
+ **Output**: &#96;ATS_PROBABILITY&#96; (HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW | NONE)
+ 
+ **Routing**:
+ - If &#96;NONE&#96; → Stop processing, archive email
+ - If &#96;HIGH&#96; or &#96;MEDIUM&#96; → Proceed to Stage 2
+ 
+ **Implementation**: See &#96;1 emailparse/score_msg.py&#96; and &#96;1 emailparse/mailscorer.py&#96;
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### Stage 2: Stage Detector
+ 
+ **Purpose**: Classify email type and determine workflow stage
+ 
+ #### 2a. Type Classification
+ 
+ Classify the email as one of three types:
+ 
+ **NEW ATS** (Completely new materials):
+ - **Field 1 (Request No.)**: Empty or not assigned (no XXX/YYYY format)
+ - **Field 51 (TKZ)**: Empty or not assigned
+ - **Form completion**: Only Fields 2-21 filled (applicant section)
+ - **Fields 22-50**: Empty (no department signatures)
+ - **Sender**: Applicant domain (not department email)
+ - **Subject**: Basic keywords, no ATS number pattern
+ 
+ **ONGOING** (New materials in process):
+ - **Field 1**: Has ATS number (XXX/YYYY format) - already assigned
+ - **Field 51**: May or may not have TKZ yet
+ - **Form completion**: Fields 22+ have some signatures (workflow in progress)
+ - **Sender**: Department email OR Standardisation Office forwarding
+ - **Subject**: Contains ATS number and/or TKZ
+ 
+ **CHANGE** (Change of existing approved material):
+ - **Field 1**: Has ATS number
+ - **Field 5**: &quot;Change in Demand&quot; checked
+ - **Field 20**: References previous ATS number
+ - **Field 51**: Has TKZ (already assigned)
+ - **Status**: Currently inactive branch - flag/tag for future handling
+ 
+ **Output**: &#96;TYPE&#96; (NEW | ONGOING | CHANGE | UNKNOWN)
+ 
+ #### 2b. Ongoing Stage Detection
+ 
+ **Only executed if &#96;TYPE = ONGOING&#96;**
+ 
+ Detect which workflow stage the application is currently at:
+ 
+ **ONGOING_STAGE_2** (ChemScan/UUB):
+ - Fields 2-24 filled (applicant + ChemScan section)
+ - Fields 25-50 empty
+ - Sender: &#96;gefahrstoffmanagement@uub-schwan.de&#96;
+ - Subject: May contain &quot;ChemScan: Stellungnahmen&quot;
+ - Attachments: ChemScan report PDF
+ 
+ **ONGOING_STAGE_3** (UWS):
+ - Fields 2-31 filled (applicant + ChemScan + UWS)
+ - Fields 32-50 empty
+ - Sender: &#96;karsten.bartz@rolls-royce.com&#96;
+ - Body: &quot;der Teil Umweltschutz der Anträge ist bearbeitet&quot;
+ - Attachments: May have &quot; (002)&quot; suffix
+ 
+ **ONGOING_STAGE_4** (HSE):
+ - Fields 2-38 filled (applicant + ChemScan + UWS + HSE)
+ - Fields 39-50 empty
+ - Sender: &#96;hse-newsou@rolls-royce.com&#96; (OU) or &#96;hs-e-teamdw@rolls-royce.com&#96; (DW)
+ - Body: &quot;anbei die Freigabe&quot; (OU) or &quot;der Antrag ist bearbeitet und freigegeben&quot; (DW)
+ 
+ **ONGOING_STAGE_5** (LAB):
+ - Fields 2-49 filled (applicant + ChemScan + UWS + HSE + LAB)
+ - Field 50 empty
+ - Sender: &#96;ralph.gross@rolls-royce.com&#96; (OU) or &#96;rrd-materials-spg@rolls-royce.com&#96; (DW)
+ 
+ **ONGOING_STAGE_6** (Final Approval):
+ - Fields 2-50 filled (all sections complete)
+ - Sender: &#96;CBS-Standardisation-Office@Rolls-Royce.com&#96;
+ 
+ **Output**: &#96;STAGE&#96; (2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | UNKNOWN)
+ 
+ **Implementation**: See &#96;1 emailparse/fromwho.py&#96; (planning notes)
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### Stage 3: Workflow Router
+ 
+ **Purpose**: Route to appropriate processing pipeline based on classification
+ 
+ **Routing Logic**:
+ 
+ | TYPE | Action |
+ |------|--------|
+ | &#96;NEW&#96; | → &#96;new_workflow&#96; pipeline |
+ | &#96;ONGOING&#96; | → &#96;ongoing_workflow&#96; with &#96;STAGE&#96; parameter |
+ | &#96;CHANGE&#96; | → Flag/tag, ignore processing (future handling) |
+ | &#96;UNKNOWN&#96; | → Manual review queue (HITL) |
+ 
+ #### NEW Workflow Pipeline
+ 
+ **Purpose**: Process completely new ATS applications
+ 
+ **Steps** (from AAW11-03, Section 01-03):
+ 1. Extract attachments to staging area
+ 2. PDF analysis: Extract all form fields (2-21)
+ 3. Validate completeness (SDS, TDS, required fields)
+ 4. Check MLC132 (prohibited substances check)
+ 5. Excel lookup: Check for duplicates in &#96;Verzeichnis.xlsb&#96;
+ 6. Generate ATS number (XXX/YYYY) from &#96;Verzeichnis.xlsb&#96;
+ 7. Generate TKZ (0104XXXX) from &#96;Teilenummern 0104....xls&#96;
+ 8. Generate response email if missing information
+ 9. Excel write: Create new entry in &#96;Verzeichnis.xlsb&#96;
+ 10. PDF write: Fill Field 1 (Request No.) and Field 51 (TKZ)
+ 11. File operations: Organize attachments
+ 12. Email (Out): Send confirmation to applicant + start ChemScan request
+ 
+ **Implementation**: See directories &#96;2 pdfparser/&#96;, &#96;3 mlc check/&#96;, &#96;5 excel/&#96;, &#96;6 files/&#96;
+ 
+ #### ONGOING Workflow Pipeline
+ 
+ **Purpose**: Process ATS applications that are in the approval workflow
+ 
+ **Steps** (from AAW11-03, Section 04-10):
+ 1. Identify current stage from classification
+ 2. Extract updated fields and signatures from PDF
+ 3. Excel lookup: Find existing entry by ATS number
+ 4. Excel write: Update status, add signatures
+ 5. PDF write: Update form with new signatures/evaluations
+ 6. File operations: Update existing files
+ 7. Email (Out): Forward to next stage (or completion notification)
+ 
+ **Stage-specific handling**:
+ - **Stage 2 (ChemScan)**: Request ChemScan evaluation, wait for response
+ - **Stage 3 (UWS)**: Forward to Environmental Protection Officer
+ - **Stage 4 (HSE)**: Forward to HSE team (OU or DW)
+ - **Stage 5 (LAB)**: Forward to Manufacturing Laboratory
+ - **Stage 6 (Final)**: Final release, update SAP, distribute notifications
+ 
+ **Implementation**: See directories &#96;2 pdfparser/&#96;, &#96;5 excel/&#96;, &#96;6 files/&#96;
+ 
+ #### CHANGE Workflow Pipeline
+ 
+ **Status**: Currently inactive
+ 
+ **Future handling**:
+ - Same process flow as NEW/ONGOING but already has ATS/TKZ pair
+ - Requires special handling for change requests
+ - Currently: Flag/tag for manual review
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ## HITL (Human-In-The-Loop) Integration
+ 
+ **Confidence Scoring**:
+ - Each classification includes a confidence score (0.0 - 1.0)
+ - Low confidence (&lt; 0.7): Flag for human review but still process
+ - Very low confidence (&lt; 0.5): Manual review queue only
+ - Human can override classification in frontend
+ 
+ **Future Enhancement**:
+ - Frontend interface for reviewing and labeling emails
+ - Background scanning with human review capability
+ - Training data collection for ML model improvement
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ## Email Processing Flow Diagram
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ Email Received
+     ↓
+ [Stage 1: ATS Detector]
+     ↓
+ ATS_PROBABILITY?
+     ├─ NONE → Archive &amp; Stop
+     └─ HIGH/MEDIUM → Continue
+     ↓
+ [Stage 2: Stage Detector]
+     ↓
+ [2a: Type Classification]
+     ↓
+ TYPE?
+     ├─ NEW → [2b: Skip] → [Stage 3: new_workflow]
+     ├─ ONGOING → [2b: Stage Detection] → [Stage 3: ongoing_workflow(STAGE)]
+     ├─ CHANGE → [2b: Skip] → Flag/Tag (Future)
+     └─ UNKNOWN → Manual Review Queue
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ## Key Form Fields Reference (T00221)
+ 
+ **Applicant Section** (Fields 2-21):
+ - Field 1: Request No. (XXX/YYYY) - Assigned by Standardisation Office
+ - Field 5: Identification of Request (New Demand / Change in Demand)
+ - Field 20: Reference to past requests
+ - Field 51: Part Number (TKZ) - Assigned by Standardisation Office
+ 
+ **Department Sections**:
+ - Fields 22-24: ChemScan (UUB)
+ - Fields 25-31: Environmental Protection Officer (UWS)
+ - Fields 32-38: Occupational Health &amp; Safety (HSE)
+ - Fields 39-49: Manufacturing Laboratory (LAB)
+ - Field 50: Standardisation Office (Final approval)
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ## Department Email Addresses
+ 
+ | Department | Email Address | Location |
+ |------------|---------------|----------|
+ | ChemScan (UUB) | gefahrstoffmanagement@uub-schwan.de | Both OU/DW |
+ | Environmental Protection (UWS) | karsten.bartz@rolls-royce.com | Both OU/DW |
+ | HSE OU | hse-newsou@rolls-royce.com | OU |
+ | HSE DW | hs-e-teamdw@rolls-royce.com | DW |
+ | LAB OU | ralph.gross@rolls-royce.com | OU |
+ | LAB DW | rrd-materials-spg@rolls-royce.com | DW |
+ | Standardisation Office | CBS-Standardisation-Office@Rolls-Royce.com | Both OU/DW |
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ## Related Documentation
+ 
+ - &#96;README.md&#96; - General workflow overview
+ - &#96;1 emailparse/README.md&#96; - Email parsing scripts documentation
+ - &#96;.docs/Forms/AAW11-03_Bearbeitung der Anträge für Teile und Stoffe-Version1.0.md&#96; - Process description
+ - &#96;.docs/Forms/01030063-AA.md&#96; - Form completion instructions
+ - &#96;.docs/instructions.md&#96; - T00221 form field descriptions
+ 
```

</details>

## Script Analysis

### **Main Workflow (`main_workflow.py`)**
Orchestrates the NEW application processing pipeline:
1. Processes PDF and extracts form data
2. Generates new IDs (TKZ + Antragsnummer)
3. Writes to Excel sheets (TKZ.xls + Verzeichnis.xlsb)

Only handles "Neubedarf" (new requirements), not "Bedarfsänderung" (changes).

---

### **ID Generator (`id_generator.py`)**
Generates sequential IDs:
- TKZ: Reads `TKZ.xls`, finds last 8-digit number (e.g., `01044397`), increments to `01044398`
- Antragsnummer: Reads `Verzeichnis.xlsb`, finds last number for current year (e.g., `158/2025`), increments to `159/2025`
- Uses COM interface to preserve Excel text formatting
- Searches from bottom-up for performance

---

### **Excel Writer (`excel_writer.py`)**
Writes extracted PDF data to Excel:
- Maps PDF fields to Excel columns using JSON mappings
- Creates rows for:
  - TKZ sheet: Teilenummer, Benennung, Antragsteller info
  - Verzeichnis sheet: Antragsnummer, TKZ, product info, location, etc.
- Detects location (OU/DW) from PDF text
- Uses COM interface to append rows sequentially

---

### **PDF Processor (`pdf_processor.py`)**
Extracts and validates PDF form data:
- Uses `pdf_fields.py` to extract form fields
- Validates it's a "Neubedarf" (rejects "Bedarfsänderung")
- Processes field values (text, buttons, signatures)
- Returns structured data ready for Excel

---

### **PDF Fields (`pdf_fields.py`)**
Low-level PDF extraction:
- Uses PyPDF2 to extract form fields
- Handles signature fields (converts binary to base64)
- Natural sorting of field names
- Can save to JSON or return in-memory

---

### **Excel Writer (`excelwriter.py`)**
Documentation file with:
- Column mappings (PDF fields → Excel columns)
- Workflow description
- Notes about NEW vs UPDATE logic

---

## Summary

This is a NEW application processing workflow that:
1. Extracts data from ATS PDF forms
2. Generates sequential IDs (TKZ + Antragsnummer)
3. Writes tracking data to Excel sheets
4. Only processes "Neubedarf" (new requirements)

Missing/not implemented:
- "Bedarfsänderung" (change requests) handling
- ONGOING workflow processing (updates to existing applications)
- Email integration (currently processes PDFs directly)
- File operations (renaming, organizing attachments)

This aligns with the NEW workflow pipeline in the architecture. It needs integration with the email processing workflow and extension to handle ONGOING applications.

+ - Extract ATS number and TKZ from existing form (Field 1, Field 51)

## How This Fits Into the Workflow

These scripts implement the NEW workflow pipeline in Stage 3 of the architecture:

```
Email → ATS Detector → Stage Detector (NEW) → Workflow Router → [Verzeichnis Scripts] → PDF Update → File Ops → Email Out
```

Currently, they handle:
- PDF extraction → ID generation → Excel writing

Missing pieces:
- Email integration (processes PDFs directly, not from emails)
- PDF updating (IDs written to Excel but not back to PDF)
- File operations (no renaming/organization)
- Email sending (no output)

## Required Modifications

### 1. ONGOING workflow support (highest priority)
- Problem: Only handles NEW (empty Field 1/51). ONGOING has existing IDs.
- Changes needed:
  - Read existing IDs from PDF (don't generate new ones)
  - Update existing Excel rows instead of creating new ones
  - Detect workflow stage from filled fields (2-24 = ChemScan, 2-31 = UWS, etc.)
  - Extract and update department signatures

### 2. CHANGE workflow support
- Problem: Currently rejects "Bedarfsänderung" applications.
- Changes needed:
  - Accept CHANGE requests (Field 5 = "Bedarfsänderung")
  - Read existing IDs from Field 1 and Field 51
  - Update specific Excel fields based on change type
  - Preserve historical data

### 3. Email integration
- Problem: Processes PDFs directly, not integrated with email workflow.
- Changes needed:
  - Extract PDF from email attachments
  - Pass email metadata (sender, subject) for stage detection
  - Handle multiple attachments (SDS, TDS, COC)

### 4. PDF updating
- Problem: IDs written to Excel but not back to PDF form.
- Changes needed:
  - Fill Field 1 (Request No.) with Antragsnummer
  - Fill Field 51 (TKZ) with generated TKZ
  - Preserve signatures and form structure

### 5. File operations
- Problem: No file renaming or organization.
- Changes needed:
  - Rename files: `XXX/YYYY_XXXXXXXX.pdf` format
  - Copy to appropriate directories (Antrag/, Sicherheitsdatenblatt/, etc.)
  - Update Excel hyperlinks

The README includes detailed modification requirements for each script. The core logic is solid; it needs workflow type detection and routing to handle NEW, ONGOING, and CHANGE.

Yes, I understand. This is a shared inbox where emails from all stages arrive continuously. The same scripts process each email based on its type and stage.

## Global Workflow Understanding

### The Continuous Loop

```
Shared Inbox (all stages)
    ↓
Email arrives (could be NEW, ONGOING Stage 2-6, or CHANGE)
    ↓
[Stage 1: ATS Detector] → Is it ATS-related?
    ↓
[Stage 2: Stage Detector] → What type? Which stage?
    ↓
[Stage 3: Workflow Router] → Route to appropriate processing
    ↓
Process (extract → Excel → PDF → send to next stage)
    ↓
Email sent to next stage
    ↓
[Wait... email comes back to shared inbox]
    ↓
[Repeat cycle]
```

### The Flow

**1. NEW ATS Incoming**
- Detect NEW (empty Field 1/51, applicant sender)
- Register: Extract PDF → Write Excel (generate IDs) → Write IDs back to PDF → Send to UUB
- Email goes to UUB inbox

**2. ONGOING ATS Incoming (from UUB)**
- Detect ONGOING Stage 2 (Fields 2-24 filled, UUB sender)
- Process: Extract updates → Write Excel (update row) → Write back to PDF → Send to UWS
- Email goes to UWS inbox

**3. ONGOING ATS Incoming (from UWS)**
- Detect ONGOING Stage 3 (Fields 2-31 filled, UWS sender)
- Process: Extract updates → Write Excel → Write back to PDF → Send to HSE
- Email goes to HSE inbox

**4. ONGOING ATS Incoming (from HSE)**
- Detect ONGOING Stage 4 (Fields 2-38 filled, HSE sender)
- Process: Extract updates → Write Excel → Write back to PDF → Send to LAB
- Email goes to LAB inbox

**5. ONGOING ATS Incoming (from LAB)**
- Detect ONGOING Stage 5 (Fields 2-49 filled, LAB sender)
- Process: Extract updates → Write Excel → Write back to PDF → Send to Final Approval
- Email goes to Standardisation Office

**6. ONGOING ATS Incoming (Final Approval)**
- Detect ONGOING Stage 6 (Fields 2-50 filled, all complete)
- Process: Final updates → Write Excel → Send approval email (broadcast)

**7. CHANGE Incoming**
- Detect CHANGE (Field 5 = "Bedarfsänderung", Field 1 has ATS number)
- Process: Special handling (currently manual)

## Key Insights

1. Shared inbox: All emails arrive in one inbox, regardless of stage.
2. Same scripts, different logic: The verzeichnis scripts are reused, but behavior changes based on:
   - Type (NEW vs ONGOING vs CHANGE)
   - Stage (2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
3. Continuous cycle: Each stage sends an email back to the inbox, triggering the next step.
4. State machine: Each ATS progresses through stages, with the system detecting where it is and what to do next.

## What This Means for the Scripts

The verzeichnis scripts need to be:

1. Type-aware:
   - NEW → Generate IDs, create new Excel rows
   - ONGOING → Read existing IDs, update existing Excel rows
   - CHANGE → Read existing IDs, special update logic

2. Stage-aware:
   - Stage 2 → Extract ChemScan fields (22-24), update specific columns
   - Stage 3 → Extract UWS fields (25-31), update specific columns
   - Stage 4 → Extract HSE fields (32-38), update specific columns
   - Stage 5 → Extract LAB fields (39-49), update specific columns
   - Stage 6 → Final processing, send approval email

3. Email-aware:
   - Extract PDF from email attachments
   - Use sender/subject for stage detection
   - Compose and send email to next stage

4. Context-aware:
   - Know where to send next (UUB → UWS → HSE → LAB → Final)
   - Know what to extract (which fields are new/updated)
   - Know what to update (which Excel columns)

The scripts are the core processing engine, but they need to be wrapped with:
- Email processing (extract attachments)
- Stage detection (determine workflow position)
- Type detection (NEW/ONGOING/CHANGE)
- Routing logic (where to send next)

File operations fit here in the workflow:

## File Operations Step - Where It Fits

### Optimal Position in Workflow:

```
1. Email (In) - Extract attachments to staging area
    ↓
2. PDF Analysis - Extract data, detect type/stage
    ↓
3. ID Generation/Reading - Get ATS number & TKZ
    ↓
4. PDF Write - Fill Field 1 & 51 with IDs
    ↓
5. FILE OPERATIONS ← HERE
   - Rename files with IDs
   - Save to shared network drive
   - Create file paths for hyperlinks
    ↓
6. Excel Write - Write data + hyperlinks (columns M-Q)
    ↓
7. Email (Out) - Attach files from network drive
```

### Why This Position?

1. After ID generation: Need ATS number (XXX/YYYY) and TKZ (XXXXXXXX) for naming
2. After PDF updating: Save the updated PDF with IDs filled in
3. Before Excel writing: Need file paths to create hyperlinks in columns M-Q
4. Before email sending: Files are organized and ready to attach

### File Operations Details

**From `renamer.py` and README:**

**File Naming Format:**
- ATS: `XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_ATS.pdf` (or `XXX/YYYY_XXXXXXXX.pdf` per README)
- SDS: `XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_SDB.pdf`
- TDS: `XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_TDB.pdf`
- COC: `XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_COC.pdf`
- TEST: `XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_TEST.pdf`

**Directory Structure (Shared Network Drive):**
- ATS: `\\network\drive\Antrag\YYYY\` (organized by year)
- SDS: `\\network\drive\Sicherheitsdatenblatt\`
- TDS: `\\network\drive\Datenblatt\`
- COC: (likely similar structure)

**Excel Hyperlinks (Verzeichnis columns):**
- Column M: Hyperlink to ATS PDF
- Column N: Hyperlink to TDS (if Field 18b = "Ja")
- Column O: Hyperlink to COC
- Column P: Hyperlink to SDS (if Field 18a = "Ja")
- Column Q: Hyperlink to Gefährdungsbeurteilung (if Field 18c = "Ja")

### Complete File Operations Step

**For NEW ATS:**
1. Extract all attachments from email (ATS form, SDS, TDS, COC, etc.)
2. Identify file types (by filename patterns or content analysis)
3. Generate IDs (XXX/YYYY, XXXXXXXXX)
4. Update PDF with IDs (Field 1, Field 51)
5. Rename files:
   - ATS: `157-2025_01044395_ATS.pdf`
   - SDS: `157-2025_01044395_SDB.pdf`
   - TDS: `157-2025_01044395_TDB.pdf`
6. Save to network drive:
   - `\\network\drive\Antrag\2025\157-2025_01044395_ATS.pdf`
   - `\\network\drive\Sicherheitsdatenblatt\157-2025_01044395_SDB.pdf`
   - `\\network\drive\Datenblatt\157-2025_01044395_TDB.pdf`
7. Create hyperlink paths for Excel
8. Write Excel with hyperlinks

**For ONGOING ATS:**
1. Extract attachments (updated ATS form, new ChemScan report, etc.)
2. Read existing IDs from PDF (Field 1, Field 51)
3. Update PDF with new signatures/evaluations
4. Rename new files with existing IDs
5. Save to network drive (may update existing files or add new ones)
6. Update Excel hyperlinks if files changed

## How SDS/TDS Detectors Fit Into the Workflow

### The Concept

**Email attachments flow:**
1. `.msg` file arrives with multiple PDF attachments
2. Extract all attachments to staging area
3. Run detectors on each PDF to identify type:
   - ATS form detector (already exists in `2 pdfparser/ats/`)
   - SDS detector (`sds_detector.py`)
   - TDS detector (`tds_detector.py`)
   - COC detector (if exists)
4. Classify each attachment → route to appropriate processing

### Current Detectors Available

**SDS Detector (`sds_detector.py`):**
- Scores PDFs 0-100 for SDS likelihood
- Detects German/English SDS documents
- Checks for SDS structure (16 sections)
- Keywords: "Sicherheitsdatenblatt", "Safety Data Sheet", GHS codes, etc.
- Returns: `SDSScore` with confidence level

**SDS Date Detector (`sds_date_detector.py`):**
- Extracts issue/revision dates from SDS
- Validates: must be <2 years old (requirement)
- Returns: validity status, expiry date

**CAS Extractor (`cas_extractor.py`):**
- Extracts CAS numbers, EC numbers from Section 3
- Used for MLC132 checking (prohibited substances)

**TDS Detector (`tds_detector.py`):**
- Scores PDFs 0-100 for TDS/PDS likelihood
- Detects Technical/Product Data Sheets
- Keywords: "Technisches Datenblatt", "Product Data Sheet", technical properties
- Excludes SDS documents (negative indicators)

### Integration into Workflow

**Step: Attachment Classification (after email extraction)**

```
Email (.msg) received
    ↓
Extract all attachments to staging area
    ↓
For each PDF attachment:
    ├─ Run ATS form detector → Is it T00221 form?
    ├─ Run SDS detector → Is it Safety Data Sheet?
    ├─ Run TDS detector → Is it Technical Data Sheet?
    └─ Run COC detector → Is it Certificate of Conformity?
    ↓
Classify attachments:
    - ATS form: [file1.pdf]
    - SDS: [file2.pdf] (score: 95/100, German, valid date)
    - TDS: [file3.pdf] (score: 82/100)
    - Unknown: [file4.pdf]
    ↓
Use classification for:
    1. File naming (XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_SDB.pdf)
    2. File organization (save to correct directories)
    3. Excel hyperlinks (columns M, N, P, Q)
    4. Validation (SDS must be German, <2 years old)
```

### Where This Fits in the Complete Workflow

**For NEW ATS:**
```
1. Email (In) - Extract attachments
2. Attachment Classification ← HERE
   - Detect ATS form
   - Detect SDS (validate: German, <2 years)
   - Detect TDS
   - Detect COC
3. PDF Analysis - Extract ATS form data
4. ID Generation - Generate TKZ + Antragsnummer
5. PDF Write - Fill Field 1 & 51
6. File Operations
   - Rename: XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_ATS.pdf
   - Rename: XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_SDB.pdf (if SDS detected)
   - Rename: XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_TDB.pdf (if TDS detected)
   - Save to network drive
7. Excel Write
   - Column M: Hyperlink to ATS PDF
   - Column P: Hyperlink to SDS (if detected + Field 18a = "Ja")
   - Column N: Hyperlink to TDS (if detected + Field 18b = "Ja")
8. Email (Out) - Attach files, send to UUB
```

**For ONGOING ATS:**
```
1. Email (In) - Extract attachments
2. Attachment Classification ← HERE
   - Detect updated ATS form (with signatures)
   - Detect new ChemScan report (Stage 2)
   - Detect other documents
3. PDF Analysis - Extract updated fields/signatures
4. Excel Update - Update existing row
5. File Operations - Update/replace files on network drive
6. Email (Out) - Forward to next stage
```

### Validation Requirements

**SDS Validation (from instructions.md):**
- Must be German language (detected by `sds_detector.py`)
- Must be <2 years old (validated by `sds_date_detector.py`)
- Must be EU-compliant (structure check)
- If invalid → Generate email to applicant requesting valid SDS

**Integration Point:**
```
After attachment classification:
    ↓
If SDS detected:
    ├─ Check language (must be German)
    ├─ Check date (must be <2 years)
    └─ If invalid → Flag for applicant notification
    ↓
If TDS detected:

  This document describes the 3-stage email processing workflow for ATS (Antrag für Teile und Stoffe) applications. The workflow is designed to automatically classify and route emails through the appropriate processing pipelines.
+ 
+ ### Global Workflow Context
+ 
+ **Shared Inbox Architecture**: All emails from all workflow stages arrive in a **shared inbox**. The system continuously monitors this inbox and processes emails based on their type and stage:
+ 
+ - **NEW ATS**: Initial application from applicant
+ - **ONGOING ATS**: Emails returning from departments (UUB, UWS, HSE, LAB, Final)
+ - **CHANGE ATS**: Change requests for existing approved materials
+ 
+ **Continuous Loop**: Each stage sends an email back to the shared inbox, which triggers the next processing step. This creates a continuous cycle where:
+ 1. Email arrives → Process → Send to next stage
+ 2. Email returns from department → Process → Send to next stage
+ 3. Repeat until final approval
+ 
+ **File System**: All files (&#96;.msg&#96;, ATS forms, SDS, TDS, COC) are stored on a **shared network drive**. Excel hyperlinks (columns M-Q in Verzeichnis) point to these files for easy access.
  
  ## Definitions

  **Purpose**: Process completely new ATS applications
  
- **Steps** (from AAW11-03, Section 01-03):
- 1. Extract attachments to staging area
- 2. PDF analysis: Extract all form fields (2-21)
- 3. Validate completeness (SDS, TDS, required fields)
- 4. Check MLC132 (prohibited substances check)

- 6. Generate ATS number (XXX/YYYY) from &#96;Verzeichnis.xlsb&#96;
- 7. Generate TKZ (0104XXXX) from &#96;Teilenummern 0104....xls&#96;
- 8. Generate response email if missing information
- 9. Excel write: Create new entry in &#96;Verzeichnis.xlsb&#96;
- 10. PDF write: Fill Field 1 (Request No.) and Field 51 (TKZ)
- 11. File operations: Organize attachments
- 12. Email (Out): Send confirmation to applicant + start ChemScan request
+ **Detailed Steps**:
+ 
+ 1. **Extract Attachments to Staging Area**
+    - Extract all PDF attachments from &#96;.msg&#96; file
+    - Save to temporary staging directory
+ 
+ 2. **Attachment Classification**
+    - Run ATS form detector (&#96;2 pdfparser/ats/&#96;) → Identify T00221 form
+    - Run SDS detector (&#96;2 pdfparser/sds/sds_detector.py&#96;) → Identify Safety Data Sheets
+    - Run TDS detector (&#96;2 pdfparser/tds/tds_detector.py&#96;) → Identify Technical Data Sheets
+    - Run COC detector (if available) → Identify Certificates of Conformity
+    - Classify each attachment: &#96;{ats_form: [path], sds: [paths], tds: [paths], coc: [paths], unknown: [paths]}&#96;
+ 
+ 3. **PDF Analysis: Extract ATS Form Data**
+    - Extract all form fields (2-21) from ATS form PDF
+    - Validate Field 5 = &quot;Neubedarf&quot; (new requirement)
+    - Extract product information, applicant details, etc.
+ 
+ 4. **SDS Validation**
+    - Check if SDS detected and Field 18a = &quot;Ja&quot; (SDS required)
+    - Validate SDS language: Must be German (detected by SDS detector)
+    - Validate SDS date: Must be &lt;2 years old (&#96;sds_date_detector.py&#96;)
+    - Extract CAS numbers for MLC132 check (&#96;cas_extractor.py&#96;)
+    - If invalid → Flag for applicant notification
+ 
+ 5. **TDS Validation**
+    - Check if TDS detected and Field 18b = &quot;Ja&quot; (TDS required)
+    - Validate TDS completeness (optional)
+ 
+ 6. **Completeness Check**
+    - Verify all required fields filled (Fields 2-21)
+    - Verify required attachments present (SDS, TDS if indicated)
+    - Generate list of missing information
+ 
+ 7. **MLC132 Check** (Prohibited Substances)
+    - Extract CAS numbers from SDS Section 3
+    - Check against MLC132 prohibited substances list
+    - If hit found → Route directly to Environmental Protection and HSE
+ 
+ 8. **Excel Lookup**
+    - Check for duplicates in &#96;Verzeichnis.xlsb&#96;
+    - Search for similar products in &#96;Teilenummern 0104....xls&#96;
+ 
+ 9. **ID Generation**
+    - Generate ATS number (XXX/YYYY) from &#96;Verzeichnis.xlsb&#96; (increment last number for current year)
+    - Generate TKZ (0104XXXX) from &#96;Teilenummern 0104....xls&#96; (increment last number)
+    - Reserve IDs (don&#39;t use until successful processing)
+ 
+ 10. **Generate Response Email** (if missing information)
+     - Create email template listing missing fields/attachments
+     - Request valid SDS (German, &lt;2 years) if invalid
+     - Request missing attachments if indicated but not provided
+ 
+ 11. **Excel Write**
+     - Create new row in &#96;Verzeichnis.xlsb&#96; with extracted data
+     - Create new row in &#96;Teilenummern 0104....xls&#96; (TKZ sheet)
+     - Write hyperlinks to files (columns M-Q) - will be filled after file operations
+ 
+ 12. **PDF Write**
+     - Fill Field 1 (Request No.) with generated Antragsnummer (XXX/YYYY)
+     - Fill Field 51 (TKZ) with generated part number (0104XXXX)
+     - Preserve all existing form data and structure
+ 
+ 13. **File Operations**
+     - Rename ATS form: &#96;XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_ATS.pdf&#96; (e.g., &#96;157-2025_01044395_ATS.pdf&#96;)
+     - Rename SDS: &#96;XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_SDB.pdf&#96; (if detected)
+     - Rename TDS: &#96;XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_TDB.pdf&#96; (if detected)
+     - Rename COC: &#96;XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_COC.pdf&#96; (if detected)
+     - Save to shared network drive:
+       - ATS: &#96;\\network\drive\Antrag\YYYY\XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_ATS.pdf&#96;
+       - SDS: &#96;\\network\drive\Sicherheitsdatenblatt\XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_SDB.pdf&#96;
+       - TDS: &#96;\\network\drive\Datenblatt\XXX-YYYY_XXXXXXXX_TDB.pdf&#96;
+     - Create file paths for Excel hyperlinks
+ 
+ 14. **Excel Hyperlink Update**
+     - Update column M: Hyperlink to ATS PDF
+     - Update column P: Hyperlink to SDS (if Field 18a = &quot;Ja&quot; and SDS detected)
+     - Update column N: Hyperlink to TDS (if Field 18b = &quot;Ja&quot; and TDS detected)
+     - Update column O: Hyperlink to COC (if detected)
+     - Update column Q: Hyperlink to Gefährdungsbeurteilung (if Field 18c = &quot;Ja&quot;)
+ 
+ 15. **Email (Out)**
+     - If missing information: Send request email to applicant
+     - If complete: Send confirmation to applicant with ATS number and TKZ
+     - Forward to UUB for ChemScan evaluation (if SDS present and MLC132 check passed)

+ - &#96;3 mlc check/&#96; - MLC132 prohibited substances check
+ - &#96;5 excel/&#96; - Excel read/write operations
+ - &#96;6 files/&#96; - File operations and renaming
